summary.text: Craig Goldman is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Texas's 12th District. A fourth-generation Fort Worth native who worked in his family's gourmet food and wine store, he served twelve years in the Texas House before winning the congressional seat in 2024. He serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and has introduced legislation with Fort Worth-area Democratic Rep. Marc Veasey, including a bill to designate a post office in memory of former Rep. Kay Granger.

paragraphs.text: Born in Texas and lives in Fort Worth. His official biography describes him as a fifth-generation Texan and fourth-generation Fort Worth native.
Earned a B.A. from the University of Texas at Austin.

Spent nearly a decade working alongside his father at the family-run gourmet food and wine store in Fort Worth, according to his official biography; Ballotpedia also lists work on political campaigns and partnerships in several real estate investment companies.
Won election to the Texas House of Representatives, District 97, in 2012 and served from 2013 to 2025, representing part of Tarrant County.
In the Texas House, held leadership positions including chairman of the House Committee on Energy Resources and chairman of the House Republican Caucus, according to his official biography.
Advanced from the March 5, 2024 Republican primary for the open 12th District seat vacated by Rep. Kay Granger, defeated John O'Shea in the May 28, 2024 primary runoff, and won the general election.
Took office in January 2025 and serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee. His district includes parts of Tarrant and Parker Counties.
In 2026, he and Rep. Marc Veasey (D-TX-33), who also represents Fort Worth, introduced the Kay Granger Post Office Act to designate a post office in memory of the former congresswoman.
